title: Composite overlap transport before projection comparison
statement: For composable scheme maps f and gk with composite g, a cartesian square for g, two opens U,V, local objects A,B and E on X with the supplied local pullback identifications, the transported gluing map psi followed by the fixed apex object comparison rho equals the constructed composite stage map, on both Boolean branches. The latter map is defined by def-pc-perfect-overlap-composite-stage-map.

source.place: Compatibility of derived pullback and open restriction; composition as in Tag 0D5S.

proof.text: The comparison constructor stores the explicit nested-site gamma. Its inverse component followed by the site overlap map is the inverse-site image of the fixed nested-square inverse, by perfectOverlapNestedSiteGamma_inv_comp. The constructor preserves the old localization lift by the proved equality API. Apply this component equation at the U and V local pullback objects.

For each branch, apply the corresponding canonical site triangle to the prescribed theta. Extract kappa as the inverse-site image of the fixed local composition comparison. Naturality of the overlap comparison moves kappa across gamma, then naturality of the site counit produces exactly the four stage-map factors.

The generic mapped-three-factor identity normalizes the map of the gluing isomorphism without simplifying the full dependent goal. Compose the equalities with the Boolean stage-map branch formula. Both branches are fully proved in the parent, with no branch modules or residual holes. Unfold only the stage-map constructor explicitly before the final definitional comparison.

proof_origin.place: Nested restriction and fixed derived pullback composition (Tag 0D5S); explicit comparison constructor repair.
proof_origin.note: Returned relabelling removed. The two clauses are proved by the existing canonical triangle and naturality APIs. The expensive localization-preimage gamma data is replaced by an explicit composite, with a fully proved agreement theorem. The stage-map branch constructor is explicitly unfolded only at the final equality.
